explanations.correct: If Chagall is in East, then Degas must be in West (they must be in different wings). This is a direct application of the different_group rule.
explanations.A: Correct. Chagall and Degas must be in different wings; if Chagall is East, Degas is West.
explanations.B: Estelle must be in East (stated rule), so she cannot be forced to West.
explanations.C: Fontaine must be in East (contrapositive of not_at West). Not necessarily forced.
explanations.D: Beatrice must be with Aubrey; they could be in East or West depending on other constraints.
explanations.E: Aubrey must be with Beatrice; placement is not forced by this local rule.

But Estelle must be in East and Fontaine must be in East, leaving only Chagall and Degas for the remaining slots. If Degas is in East, then Chagall must be in West (different_group). But then West has Aubrey, Beatrice, and Chagall (3 paintings), and East has Estelle, Fontaine, and Degas (3 paintings). This is actually consistent. Let me recalculate: if Aubrey in West, Beatrice in West, Estelle in East, Fontaine in East, Degas in East, then Chagall must be in West. But West has 4 paintings. Contradiction. So (B) cannot be true.
